question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [Territorial exchanges under the Treaty of Aix-la-Chapelle (1748)]
options: Madras (Fort St. George) — Restored to Great Britain by the French
Louisbourg (North America) — Restored to France by the British in exchange for Madras
Pondicherry — Placed under joint Anglo-French administration to prevent future conflicts
Parma and Piacenza (Italy) — Ceded to Spanish Bourbon prince Philip in the European settlement
wrong_fact: Pondicherry was not placed under joint Anglo-French administration. It remained the sovereign and exclusive headquarters of the French East India Company under Governor-General Dupleix.
explanation: The Treaty of Aix-la-Chapelle (1748) ended the War of Austrian Succession. Its main global clause involved a direct swap: Madras in India was returned to the British, while the fortress of Louisbourg in Nova Scotia (North America) was returned to the French. In Europe, the Duchies of Parma, Piacenza, and Guastalla were ceded to Spain. Pondicherry remained entirely French and was never subject to joint administration.

question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [Geographic scope and impact of the Treaty of Aix-la-Chapelle in India]
options: Fort St. David (Cuddalore) — Reverted to its status as a subordinate factory under Madras after Madras was restored in 1749
Madras — Officially handed back to the British in August 1749, ending nearly three years of French occupation
Karikal — French possession in Tanjore territory that had to be surrendered to the British under the treaty
Austrian Netherlands (Flanders) — Restored to Austria by France, mirroring the return of Madras in India
wrong_fact: Karikal was not surrendered to the British. It remained a French possession, as the treaty stipulated a mutual restoration of conquests made during the war (Madras for Louisbourg), leaving other pre-war enclaves like Karikal unaffected.
explanation: Under the Treaty of Aix-la-Chapelle, only wartime conquests were exchanged (Madras returned to the British in August 1749, while the British returned Louisbourg). Fort St. David, which served as the British headquarters during the occupation, returned to its subordinate status. In Europe, France evacuated the Austrian Netherlands. Karikal, acquired by the French in 1739 before the war, remained French.

question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [Global geopolitical coordinates of the Treaty of Aix-la-Chapelle, 1748]
options: Aix-la-Chapelle (Aachen) — Imperial city in western Germany where the peace congress was held
Madras (Coromandel Coast) — Exchanged for Louisbourg (Cape Breton Island, Canada)
Madras and Fort St. David boundary — Demarcated by a joint commission along the Palar River in 1749
Assiento (Slave Trade Monopoly) — British monopoly contract in Spanish America renewed for four years under the treaty
wrong_fact: The boundary between Madras and Fort St. David was not demarcated along the Palar River. Fort St. David (Cuddalore) lies about 180 km south of Madras, separated by various territories; no such joint boundary demarcation along the Palar River took place under the treaty.
explanation: The Treaty of Aix-la-Chapelle was signed in Aachen (Aix-la-Chapelle). The global deal swapped Madras for Louisbourg in Canada. The treaty also renewed Great Britain's lucrative Assiento contract with Spain for four years. The boundary between Madras and Fort St. David (Cuddalore) was never demarcated along the Palar River, as they were separate coastal enclaves surrounded by the Nawab of Arcot's territories.
